newsitem.title: CANADA: Noranda Brunswick deal ratified - union.
newsitem.headline: Noranda Brunswick deal ratified - union.

text.p: New collective agreements between Noranda Inc and 1300 unionized employees at its Brunswick Mining and Smelting subsidiary were ratified by a member vote, union officials said.
The contracts provide for wage increases over three years and pension plan improvements, the United Steelworkers of America said in a statement.

The Brunswick mining division produced 252,834 tonnes of zinc in 1996, while the Brunswick smelter produced 71,750 tonnes of lead last year. Contract talks are continuing at Noranda's Heath Steele operation, the union said.
The Heath zinc and lead operation produced 50,813 tonnes of zinc and 6,016 tonnes of lead in 1996.
The contracts at the Brunswick mine and smelter provide for wage increases ranging between C$0.90 and C$1.53 an hour, with an average increase of C$1.26 an hour.
Improvements to the pension plans total 20 per cent over the life of the agreements and there is a special early retirement window for each of the three years in the event of a downsizing.
